- Provide a per-org token/meters breakdown for the billing period (May 20 - Jun 19)
- Confirm how VAT was applied and whether reverse-charge should have been used on the EU portion
- Share the raw metering export or a CSV we can reconcile against our logs

We’re prepping the finance team for month-end and need to know whether to request a credit or reclassification. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,

Olga / team — I pulled the export and did a quick pass. Attaching the CSV: quantisys_metering_20260619.csv (first tab: per-request rows; second tab: aggregated by org-id). Quick notes: 

- Raw counts: 92,430 total tokens in period. Attribution breakdown in the export shows ~27% (25,076 tokens) mapped to org-id-qa (EU), ~63% (58,269) to quantisys-main, remainder to service accounts.
- Root cause: looks like a shared API key was used by a staging service that reports under the parent org. Our attribution logic currently maps by API key first, then falls back to org metadata; because the staging key is registered to quantisys-main, those calls show up there.
- Impact: if we reattribute by org-id present in the payload (our secondary heuristic), we should move ~22k tokens to the EU org — equivalent to $210. Attached is a proposed credit calc (proposed_credit_calc.xlsx) with line items for token reallocation and VAT reclassification.

Next steps I propose:
- We send Quantisys the CSV and explain the shared-key attribution issue.
- If they confirm the EU traffic belongs to org-id-qa, we issue a pro-rated credit for the tokens and reverse-charge VAT on that portion (pending Laura’s confirmation).

Attachments: quantisys_metering_20260619.csv; proposed_credit_calc.xlsx

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick flag and for your patience while we reviewed. Short summary and proposal below.

What we found:
- Our metering export (attached) shows ~92.4k tokens for the billing window. Roughly 27% of those tokens originated from org-id-qa (your EU subsidiary), but were billed to quantisys-main due to a shared API key that’s registered to your parent org.
- The token attribution logic used for billing prefers API key registration metadata over payload org-id, which caused the EU traffic to be billed to the parent.

What we propose:
1) Recalculate and reallocate tokens: move the 25,076 tokens to org-id-qa and reissue an adjusted invoice line for the period.
2) Pro-rated credit: issue a credit of $210 (see attached proposed_credit_calc.xlsx) applied to your next invoice.
3) VAT treatment: if Quantisys confirms the EU entity is the supplier of the traffic and provides a VAT registration ID, we will reverse-charge the VAT on the reallocated portion and reissue the VAT summary. Laura, can you confirm exactly which supporting docs we need from the customer to complete the reverse-charge?

If you’re good with this path, I’ll coordinate the credit and updated invoice. We can also schedule a short call to walk through the CSV and the attribution logic so your finance team can reconcile it against your logs.

Next steps / asks for Quantisys:
- Reply to confirm the 3 bullet points above and attach the EU VAT registration ID (if applicable).
- If you prefer a call, propose 30 minutes this week and we’ll coordinate.

Thanks,
